approach: Smartkin's C++ decompilation built natively on HAB3X's SDL3 platform layer, which emulates the PS2's graphics (GS, VIF, VU1) with an OpenGL renderer; the Windows port adds Windows' calling convention, the low memory emulation, three threads and the crash fixes.

notes: Plays from start to credits, played by hand and by testers. A steady 60 fps, or 50, 120, 144 Hz and unlimited at the same game speed; up to 8x the PS2's resolution with FXAA, SMAA or supersampling, anisotropic filtering, the characters drawn as on the PS2, widescreen, 21:9 and 32:9, a draw distance and a dithering option; keyboard, mouse and controllers with their own button prompts; a PC options screen with separate text and voice languages; game options, off by default (infinite lives, a stronger Aku Aku, the slide jump at any moment, level select, a speedrun timer, a drop shadow), an optional cutscene skip and the retail bug fixes; mods (Crate Mod Loader's Mod Crates, and zips or modified disc images imported as only what they change) and PCSX2's texture packs; a Linux AppImage with the Steam Deck's defaults (not tried on a Deck yet). The SHA-1 is of the disc's executable, SLES_525.68, which the program checks, not of the disc image. Next: the North American v2.00 disc and a faster renderer as an option for weaker PCs.
